key_insight: General-purpose LLMs could identify some psychosis symptoms from clinical notes, but overall performance was only poor to moderate and better for positive than negative symptoms.
clinical_relevance: This suggests LLMs are not yet reliable for clinical use in psychosis phenotyping, though they may still support exploratory research in large cohorts.
method: Task: extract 8 schizophrenia symptoms from clinical summaries
Compared performance with gold-standard annotations and regression analyses
evidence_signal: In a severe mental illness cohort of 704 patients, macro F1 ranged from 0.500 to 0.647, and few-shot prompting did not significantly improve results.
watch_item: Extraction errors can distort symptom patterns, especially for negative symptoms, creating a risk of systematic bias in downstream analyses.
paper_title: Extracting Symptoms of Psychotic Disorders from Clinical Notes using Natural Language Processing.
